implementation_summary: Sender (inviteContext.ts): createInviteContextSender sends one extensions.sendInboxRumor of kind 21064 (APP_INBOX_KINDS.inviteContext) with content exactly {groupId,name} after a delivered/retryable invite outcome (rumor id = NIP-01 hash), nothing for failed/declined/error values, never throws; createContextSendingInviter decorates the S8 inviter and does not await the context send. Name handling: sanitizeContextName (NFC, invisible format characters removed with ZWJ kept between emoji, controls to space, grapheme-boundary 64 code-point cap, markup literal) and strict parseInviteContextContent that never carries extra keys. Store (inviteContextStore.ts): per-account holding store keyed groupId+sender, dedupe by rumor id (plus bounded tombstones of discarded ids), whole-snapshot port persistence ordered by persisted seq, 8 per sender / 64 total (strangers evicted before trusted, oldest first) / 7 days over unmatched contexts, sponsor validation against sponsorAccount/sponsors on arrival, matched contexts deleted when their invitation leaves pending(); bindInviteContextToPendingView reconciles on view.onChange, withInviteContextCleanup discards on successful accept/decline. Handler (inviteContextHandler.ts): drops wrong kind, non-64-hex sender, blocked sender (DenyLayer.isBlocked before anything is stored), malformed payload; persist-and-return, no client call, store errors reported not thrown. View model (invitationCardViewModel.ts): pure {invitationId, displayName, nameSource, sponsorAccount}; name only from a sponsor context, else the generic i18n label; no description/admin fields. InvitationCard gets an optional viewModel prop (legacy Welcome decode remains the fallback until the S18 cut-over). Production IDB adapter in app/src/lib/marmot/inviteContextIdbPort.ts.

decisions: Generic label reuses the existing i18n key copy.groups.pendingInvitations.unknownGroupFallback (en 'Group invitation', de 'Gruppeneinladung'); no new string was needed, so i18n.ts is unchanged. A test pins both languages.

The IndexedDB adapter lives in app/src/lib/marmot/inviteContextIdbPort.ts, outside scope.includes, because the S9 structural scan (pendingView.test.ts) forbids any idb-keyval import inside app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/. The store stays pure behind an injected load/save port.

Caps (8/64) apply only to HELD (unmatched) contexts, per the AC wording 'contexts with no matching invitation'; a context validated against a pending invitation is exempt and bounded by the invitation caps, so a stranger flood cannot evict a real invitation's name. Age order is the insertion seq, not the sender's created_at.
Expiry is measured from local arrival time (injected clock) and is strict: kept at exactly 7 days, gone at 7 days + 1 ms.
A later rumor with the same groupId+sender replaces the earlier name (keyed by groupId+sender); the same rumor id is a no-op even without a stored key match.
Sender sanitises the name with the same function as the receiver and sends nothing when it sanitises to empty (card keeps the generic label); a normal name is sent verbatim.

Payload extra keys are ignored and never stored (rather than rejecting the rumor), so a sender-added description cannot reach any model; parsing requires a hex groupId (<=128) and a non-empty sanitised name.
InvitationCard.tsx takes an optional viewModel prop; without it the legacy Welcome-decode path is unchanged. The production composition is intentionally not done here (see limitations).

Name sanitising (remediation): NFC first; C0/C1 controls and line separators become a space; every Unicode format character (Cf) plus blank fillers (U+115F/1160/3164/FFA0/2800/180E/00AD/061C/FFF9-FFFB, tag range) is REMOVED, not spaced; a ZWJ is kept only between Extended_Pictographic code points (family, rainbow flag, professions round-trip); at most 4 combining marks per base; a name with no visible character is empty (generic label); the 64 cap is in code points and cuts on a grapheme boundary via Intl.Segmenter (code-point fallback). MAX_CONTEXT_NAME_LENGTH is asserted equal to MAX_GROUP_NAME_LENGTH (units differ: code points vs UTF-16, so a valid group name always fits).

createContextSendingInviter returns the invite result immediately: the context send is started, not awaited, and every failure (target read, rumor build, sync throw, rejection) is routed to onError; the send promise is exposed through the optional onContextSend hook for callers and tests.
The sender lowercases the invitee pubkey and reports a 'failed' delivery status through onError with the reason only (never the content or name).

Held-context eviction at the 64 total cap is trust-ranked: the store takes the same isTrustedSponsor predicate as the pending view and evicts strangers before trusted senders, oldest first within a class (a throwing predicate counts as a stranger).
Discarded contexts (accept/decline discard, matched context leaving pending) leave a bounded (256) tombstone of the rumor id with the 7-day TTL, so a redelivery is 'duplicate'.

A failed port.load clears the memoised load so the next call retries; nothing is persisted until a load succeeded; a successful retry merges the contexts accepted in memory meanwhile after the stored ones under fresh seqs.
InvitationCard ignores a view model whose invitationId differs from the invitation and skips the legacy Welcome decode whenever a matching view model is supplied (selectCardViewModel, pure).

ZWNJ (U+200C) rule: kept only when it sits between two letters (\p{L}, combining marks attached to the first are transparent), exactly like ZWJ between pictographs, because it is orthographically required in Persian and several Indic scripts; removed when leading, trailing, next to a space/digit/punctuation, or doubled (a doubled ZWNJ drops both; chosen over collapsing to one for simplicity and predictability). The rule is script-agnostic: a ZWNJ between two Latin letters is also kept.
limitations: Not wired into production: registering createInviteContextHandler as inboxHandlers.inviteContext at bootstrap, constructing the store with createIdbInviteContextPort + view.pending, calling bindInviteContextToPendingView.reconcileNow() after view.seed(), passing viewModel to InvitationCard and swapping the invite call site to createContextSendingInviter all belong to the production cut-over (S18-marmot-context-cutover); the harness proves the composition works end to end.
e2e halves of AC-CTX-2/5 (groups-invitation-preview rewrite) run in S26.
A context that arrives after its invitation was capped out or declined is held up to 7 days as an unmatched context (bounded by the held caps), never shown.
Before the S18 cut-over the card has no live subscription: consumers must re-render on InviteContextStore.subscribe and PendingInvitationView.onChange.
Tombstones are in memory only: a redelivery of a discarded rumor after an app reload is not suppressed by the store (the library's own inbox dedupe is the first line).
Tag characters are stripped, so emoji subdivision flags (England, Scotland, Wales) lose their tag sequence and show as the base flag.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The S9 structural scan (pendingView.test.ts) bans idb-keyval imports anywhere in app/src/lib/marmot/invitations/, which is not stated in the story scope; a store with its own persistence only found out via a full-suite failure, forcing the adapter outside scope.includes.
retrospective.surprised_by: A file-level unicode escape written through a heredoc was materialised as literal U+2028 characters and broke the regex literal; escapes had to be built with chr().
